brief: The bottom band of every frame is a flat black bar, and it is drawn on purpose by drawSill(). Measured on HEAD this pass, seed 42 simT 175 (day 4, 10:36, daylight 0.90), deviceScaleFactor 1: sampling the canvas below sillTop(), min luma == max luma == mean == 8.4 at 1200x720, 1600x950 AND 390x844 - a perfectly uniform fill, 0 pixels above luma 20 out of 42,624 / 62,628 / 6,358. At daylight 0.37 it is 6.2 flat; at 0.00, 3.0 flat. The strip is max(26, H*0.075), 5.8-7.2% of every frame. drawSill's own features - a 2.2 px lit front edge, two geranium pots and a cup at 5.5% and 94.5% of W - are silhouetted in rgba(9,8,6) against a #0a0806 ground, under one luma unit apart, so the sill this whole domain is named after cannot be seen. Above it the apron compounds the problem at small sizes: at 1600x950 its gradient ramps 123-109-99-89-82 and then cliffs to 8, but at 1200x720 that ramp is one row (119 -> 45 -> 8), so the near roof reads as a thin grey strip over a black bar. Make the bottom band read as a windowsill in shadow - a surface with a near edge, some depth, and something standing on it. Note drawSill runs inside drawOurSide, which runs inside drawGround: it is baked into the GROUND CACHE, so anything per-frame there has to be a live overlay.
successLooksLike: At 1200x720 DSF1, seed 42 t=175, the strip below sillTop() has an internal luma RANGE of at least 12 where HEAD's is exactly 0.0, and the pots and cup are findable in a difference image against HEAD. The band still reads clearly darker than the roof above it at every hour you sample, and the roof-apron-sill transition is a gradient rather than a cliff at 1200x720.
avoid: Do NOT just raise the brightness. #100's finding stands and is why the band is dark: a dark near block is what lets the town read past it. The fix is value SEPARATION inside a dark band - a real dark surface still shows 15-30 luma of internal range - not a higher mean. Do not change sillTop()'s formula without checking viewFor(), which reads it as the ONE definition and prices the camera against it.
